guard: every tool handed pi.registerTool is a closed object whose JSON round-trip carries only JSON Schema keywords — no vendor brand survives stringify (#1835)
why: THE BRAND CAME BACK ONCE ALREADY. The original converter branded Zod's JSON Schema render with
`Type.Unsafe`, and the brand's clone made Zod's non-enumerable `~standard` metadata enumerable,
so every tool's parameters serialized with `~standard.{vendor,version}` and strict providers
refused the whole declaration. A converter can re-grow that wrapper for the best of reasons
(TSchema looks like it wants a TypeBox value), which is why the guard lives at the seam pi owns:
P1 RESTORES THE #1835 DEFECT VERBATIM, import and call in one span: re-introducing the call
without its `Type` import is a ReferenceError the suite dies in before any cell, an unrelated
red, so the mutation carries both halves of the pre-fix shape. It must redden the round-trip
cell, whose stray-path list is the direct measurement of the provider-facing leak; closure
cells stay green under it, exactly as they did at base — the defect is orthogonal to closure,
and a mutation that reddened a closure cell would be proving a different regression.
P2 IS THE SUBTLER RE-INTRODUCTION: not the brand, but an ordinary enumerable member smuggled
onto the render. It proves the cell walks ALL keys at every depth rather than matching the one
string `~standard` — a cell that special-cased yesterday's key name would pass the next
vendor's metadata member straight through to the provider.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports the extension's src through tsx and registers tools against a
fake ExtensionAPI, so there is no dist/ copy that could disagree with the mutation.

mutations.name: P1 the Type.Unsafe brand returns (the #1835 defect verbatim)
mutations.expectRed: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.cell: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.note: The code-only return-line mutation calls Type.Unsafe through Node’s built-in createRequire, so the fixture restores the exact branded shape without needing a second import edit or anchoring across comments. The brand’s clone makes Zod’s non-enumerable ~standard enumerable, so stringify carries parameters(cotal_*).~standard for all 22 tools and the round-trip cell names every path.
